title: Professional Employee Performance Write-Up Template

intro: A professional employee performance write-up helps managers document performance discussions clearly, fairly, and constructively while creating actionable development plans and maintaining consistent workplace expectations. whenToUse: Use this template during performance reviews, coaching sessions, corrective action discussions, improvement plans, probationary evaluations, annual reviews, disciplinary documentation, or employee development meetings.

tips: Use objective examples and measurable data whenever possible.
Focus feedback on observable behaviors rather than personal traits.
Avoid introducing surprise issues that were never previously discussed.
Include actionable improvement plans with timelines and support.
Allow employees space to provide comments or clarification.

faqs.question: What is an employee performance write-up?
faqs.answer: An employee performance write-up is a formal document used to record performance feedback, accomplishments, concerns, and improvement expectations.

faqs.question: What is the SBI feedback framework?
faqs.answer: SBI stands for Situation, Behavior, and Impact, a structured method used to provide objective and actionable performance feedback.

faqs.question: Why should performance reviews include measurable data?
faqs.answer: Objective metrics help reduce bias, improve fairness, and provide clearer performance expectations.

faqs.question: Should employees be allowed to respond to write-ups?
faqs.answer: Yes, providing space for employee comments supports transparency, fairness, and two-way communication.

faqs.question: Why are action plans important in performance write-ups?
faqs.answer: Action plans help employees understand expectations, timelines, support resources, and measurable improvement goals.

title: Professional PTO Request Email Template
description: Free professional PTO request email template for vacation requests, paid time off, personal leave, and workplace scheduling. Copy, customize, and download instantly.
intro: A professional PTO request email helps employees request vacation time or personal leave clearly while minimizing workflow disruptions and maintaining strong workplace communication. This template is designed to improve approval speed by presenting leave dates upfront, outlining coverage plans, and demonstrating thoughtful preparation before time away from work.
whenToUse: Use this template when requesting paid time off for vacations, personal leave, family travel, rest and recovery, appointments, short-term absences, or other planned time away from work.
template:
SUBJECT: PTO Request – [Your Name] – [Start Date] through [End Date]

Dear [Manager or Supervisor Name],

I hope you are doing well.

I am writing to formally request paid time off from [Start Date] through [End Date]. I plan to return to work on [Return Date].

Reason for Leave (Optional):
[Vacation / Personal travel / Family event / Personal time / Rest and recovery / Other brief explanation]

To help ensure a smooth workflow during my absence, I will complete all priority assignments and organize coverage for ongoing responsibilities before my leave begins.

Coverage Plan:

- [Colleague Name] will assist with [tasks or responsibilities]
- Pending projects will be updated before departure
- Important files and status updates will be documented
- Client or team communications will be addressed before leave begins

Availability During Leave:

[ ] I will have limited access to email.
[ ] I will be unavailable during this time.
[ ] For urgent matters only, I may be reached at:
[Phone Number or Email]

I have reviewed current team schedules and deadlines and believe this timeframe will minimize disruption to ongoing operations.

If approved, I will also ensure the request is submitted through the company’s official HR or payroll system if required.

Please let me know if you need any additional information or if there are any concerns regarding these dates.

Thank you very much for your time and consideration.

Best regards,

[Your Full Name]
[Job Title]
[Department]
[Phone Number]
[Email Address]
example:
SUBJECT: PTO Request – Taylor Morgan – July 8 through July 15

Dear Sarah,

I hope you are doing well.

I am writing to formally request paid time off from July 8, 2027 through July 15, 2027. I plan to return to work on July 16, 2027.

I will be traveling with family during this time.

Before my departure, I will complete all open client deliverables and finalize status updates for ongoing projects.

Coverage Plan:

- Jordan Lee will monitor incoming client requests
- Weekly reports will be submitted before departure
- Shared project files will be fully updated

Availability During Leave:

I will have limited access to email during this time, but for urgent matters I can be reached by phone.

I have reviewed the current team schedule and do not anticipate any conflicts with major project deadlines.

Please let me know if these dates work for the team schedule or if you need any additional information.

Thank you very much for considering my request.

Best regards,

Taylor Morgan
Operations Coordinator
tips: Submit PTO requests as early as possible whenever dates are known.
Clearly state your requested dates near the beginning of the email.
Provide a thoughtful workload coverage plan before taking leave.
Check company PTO procedures and HR systems before submitting requests.
Avoid oversharing personal details unrelated to the request.

faqs.question: What is a PTO request email?
faqs.answer: A PTO request email is a professional message used to formally request paid time off or planned leave from work.

faqs.question: How far in advance should PTO requests be submitted?
faqs.answer: Many employers encourage employees to submit PTO requests several weeks in advance whenever possible.

faqs.question: Should PTO requests include a reason for leave?
faqs.answer: Providing a brief reason can be helpful, but extensive personal details are usually unnecessary.

faqs.question: Why is a coverage plan important in PTO requests?
faqs.answer: A coverage plan demonstrates professionalism and helps minimize workflow disruptions during an employee’s absence.

faqs.question: Should PTO requests also be entered into HR systems?
faqs.answer: Many companies require PTO requests to be submitted through official HR or payroll platforms in addition to email approval.

faqs.question: What is an employee attendance write-up?
faqs.answer: An employee attendance write-up is a formal document used to address attendance-related policy violations such as tardiness, absenteeism, or no-call no-shows.

faqs.question: When should attendance issues become formal write-ups?
faqs.answer: Formal write-ups are often used after repeated attendance problems, failed coaching efforts, serious no-call no-show incidents, or ongoing policy violations.

faqs.question: Why should attendance write-ups include specific dates and times?
faqs.answer: Specific documentation helps ensure fairness, consistency, legal compliance, and accurate performance tracking.

faqs.question: Can attendance discipline apply to protected leave situations?
faqs.answer: Protected leave categories such as FMLA, ADA accommodations, or legally protected sick leave may require separate review before disciplinary action is taken.

faqs.question: Why are improvement plans important in attendance write-ups?
faqs.answer: Improvement plans clarify expectations, support employee accountability, and provide measurable opportunities for corrective progress.

title: Professional PTO Request Denial Letter Template
description: Free professional PTO request denial letter template for managers, HR teams, and supervisors handling vacation requests, scheduling conflicts, and staffing coverage issues.
intro: A professional PTO request denial letter helps managers communicate scheduling decisions clearly, fairly, and respectfully while protecting workplace morale and maintaining operational coverage. This template is designed to support transparent communication, policy consistency, legal awareness, and employee trust by balancing business needs with empathy and alternative scheduling options.
whenToUse: Use this template when declining vacation requests, PTO requests, leave requests, blackout-period absences, overlapping team vacations, or scheduling conflicts that create operational challenges or staffing shortages.
template:
SUBJECT: Regarding Your PTO Request for [Requested Dates]

Dear [Employee Name],

Thank you for submitting your paid time off request for [Requested Dates]. I appreciate you providing advance notice and planning ahead.

After reviewing current staffing levels, project timelines, departmental coverage, and operational needs, we are unfortunately unable to approve your request for the requested dates.

Reason for Denial:

[Examples]
- Critical business deadlines
- Peak operational season
- Existing approved employee absences
- Staffing coverage limitations
- Blackout period restrictions
- Major client or project commitments
- Compliance or scheduling requirements

At this time, your role and responsibilities are necessary to support ongoing operations during this period.

Alternative Options:

We would be happy to discuss alternative time-off dates, including:

- [Alternative Date Option 1]
- [Alternative Date Option 2]
- Partial PTO arrangements
- Adjusted scheduling options

We understand the importance of personal time, rest, and work-life balance, and this decision is based solely on operational scheduling needs during the requested timeframe.

If you would like to discuss other scheduling options or future PTO availability, please feel free to schedule time with me.

Thank you for your understanding, flexibility, and continued contributions to the team.

Best regards,

[Manager Name]
[Job Title]
[Department]
[Company Name]
[Phone Number]
[Email Address]

IMPORTANT HR AND COMPLIANCE NOTE:

Vacation or general PTO requests may be subject to scheduling approval and operational requirements depending on company policy and local labor laws. However, legally protected leave categories — including qualifying paid sick leave, protected medical leave, ADA accommodations, or FMLA-related leave — may be governed by separate legal requirements and should be reviewed carefully with HR or legal counsel before denial.
example:
SUBJECT: Regarding Your PTO Request for July 15 – July 19

Dear Taylor,

Thank you for submitting your paid time off request for July 15 through July 19. I appreciate you providing advance notice.

After reviewing current project schedules and staffing coverage, we are unfortunately unable to approve PTO during this specific week.

The operations department will be supporting a major client system migration during this period, and multiple team members already have approved leave scheduled. Your project expertise and support coverage are necessary to help ensure successful completion of the transition.

Alternative Options:

We would be happy to approve PTO for one of the following alternative periods:

- July 29 – August 2
- August 12 – August 16

We understand the importance of taking time away from work to recharge, and this decision is based entirely on operational scheduling needs.

Please let me know if either alternative timeframe may work for you, and we can review scheduling together.

Thank you for your understanding and continued hard work.

Best regards,

Jordan Lee
Operations Manager
tips: Respond to PTO requests promptly so employees can adjust plans if necessary.
Apply PTO approval and denial policies consistently across all employees.
Clearly explain the operational reason for the denial without sounding punitive.
Offer alternative dates or flexible scheduling options whenever possible.
Review local leave laws carefully before denying protected leave categories.

faqs.question: Can employers deny vacation or PTO requests?
faqs.answer: In many workplaces, employers may deny vacation or PTO requests based on operational needs, staffing coverage, scheduling conflicts, or company policy.

faqs.question: Should managers explain why a PTO request was denied?
faqs.answer: Yes. Providing a clear and respectful explanation improves transparency, fairness, and employee trust.

faqs.question: Why should alternative dates be offered?
faqs.answer: Offering alternative dates shows flexibility and demonstrates that employee rest and work-life balance are still valued.

faqs.question: Can legally protected leave be denied?
faqs.answer: Certain leave categories, such as qualifying sick leave, FMLA leave, ADA accommodations, or protected medical leave, may be subject to separate legal protections and should be reviewed carefully.

faqs.question: Why is documentation important when denying PTO?
faqs.answer: Consistent documentation helps support fairness, operational decision-making, and legal compliance while maintaining an audit trail.

title: Professional Contract Extension Letter Template
description: Free professional contract extension letter template for extending business, employment, service, lease, vendor, consulting, or partnership agreements with updated timelines and terms.
intro: A contract extension letter formally extends the term of an existing agreement while preserving legal clarity and protecting both parties. This template is designed for professional use across business services, employment agreements, consulting engagements, leases, vendor relationships, and project-based contracts. It clearly references the original agreement, establishes the new contract period, outlines any revised terms, and provides signature acceptance for enforceability.
whenToUse: Use this template when extending the duration of an existing contract before its expiration date, including service agreements, employment contracts, leases, consulting arrangements, maintenance agreements, vendor partnerships, or ongoing project engagements.
template:
CONTRACT EXTENSION LETTER

[Your Company Name]
[Your Address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone Number]
[Email Address]

Date: [MM/DD/YYYY]

TO:
[Recipient Name]
[Recipient Title]
[Recipient Company Name]
[Recipient Address]
[City, State ZIP]

Subject: Contract Extension for [Original Contract Name or Reference Number]

Dear [Recipient Name],

This letter serves as a formal agreement to extend the terms of the existing contract titled "[Original Contract Name]" originally executed on [Original Contract Date] between [Your Company Name] and [Recipient Company or Individual Name].

The parties mutually agree to extend the contract term for an additional period of [Extension Duration]. The extended contract term shall begin on [New Start Date] and continue through [New End Date], unless terminated earlier in accordance with the original agreement or this extension letter.

1. ORIGINAL AGREEMENT REFERENCE

Original Contract Name: [Contract Title]
Original Effective Date: [MM/DD/YYYY]
Original Expiration Date: [MM/DD/YYYY]
Contract or Reference Number: [Reference Number]

2. EXTENSION PERIOD

Extended Contract Start Date: [MM/DD/YYYY]
Extended Contract End Date: [MM/DD/YYYY]

3. TERMS AND CONDITIONS

Except as specifically modified in this extension letter, all terms, conditions, obligations, rights, warranties, confidentiality provisions, indemnification clauses, dispute resolution procedures, and other provisions contained within the original agreement shall remain unchanged and in full force and effect throughout the extension period.

4. MODIFICATIONS TO ORIGINAL AGREEMENT

[Select one]

[ ] No modifications are being made to the original agreement.

[ ] The following provisions are amended during the extension period:

- Compensation or pricing adjustment: [Describe updated pricing, rates, or payment terms]
- Revised deliverables or scope: [Describe changes]
- Updated milestones or deadlines: [Describe revisions]
- Renewal or termination updates: [Describe modifications]
- Additional provisions: [Describe additional terms]

5. EFFECTIVE DATE

This contract extension shall become effective upon execution by both parties.

6. TERMINATION

All termination rights and notice provisions contained in the original agreement shall continue to apply during the extension period unless otherwise modified herein.

7. ENTIRE AGREEMENT

This extension letter, together with the original agreement, constitutes the entire understanding between the parties regarding the extension of the contract term. In the event of any conflict between this extension and the original agreement, the terms of this extension shall control solely with respect to the modified provisions.

8. COUNTERPARTS AND ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES

This extension may be executed in counterparts and delivered electronically. Electronic signatures shall be considered legally binding to the same extent as original signatures.

9. ACCEPTANCE DEADLINE

To confirm acceptance of this extension, please sign and return a copy of this letter no later than [Deadline Date].

We appreciate the opportunity to continue our professional relationship and look forward to a successful extension of our agreement.

Sincerely,

__________________________________
[Your Name]
[Your Title]
[Company Name]
Date: ****************************


ACCEPTANCE OF CONTRACT EXTENSION

The undersigned acknowledges and agrees to the terms of this Contract Extension Letter.

****************************______
[Recipient Name]
[Recipient Title]
[Recipient Company Name]
Date: ****************************

10. OPTIONAL LEGAL CLAUSES

Force Majeure:
Neither party shall be liable for delays or failure to perform caused by circumstances beyond reasonable control, including natural disasters, government actions, labor disputes, or other force majeure events.

Severability:
If any provision of this extension is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain valid and enforceable.

Survival:
Confidentiality, indemnification, intellectual property, payment obligations, and dispute resolution provisions shall survive expiration or termination of the agreement where applicable.

tips: Extend contracts before the original expiration date whenever possible.
Clearly reference the exact original contract title and execution date.
Specify whether original terms remain unchanged or are being modified.
Use precise start and end dates for the extension period.
Include signature acceptance blocks for both parties to ensure enforceability.

faqs.question: What is a contract extension letter?
faqs.answer: A contract extension letter is a formal agreement used to extend the duration of an existing contract while preserving or modifying its original terms.

faqs.question: Can contract terms change during an extension?
faqs.answer: Yes. Parties may extend the timeline while also modifying pricing, deliverables, deadlines, or other agreed provisions.

faqs.question: Should a contract extension be signed by both parties?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both parties should sign the extension letter to confirm mutual agreement and legal enforceability.

faqs.question: When should a contract extension be used?
faqs.answer: A contract extension should generally be completed before the original agreement expires.

faqs.question: What happens if the original contract already expired?
faqs.answer: If the original contract has already expired, parties may need a new agreement or legal review rather than a simple extension letter.
